name: OMBR automation syntax rover
description: Illustrative, non-deployable automation manifest showing mechanical source catalogs and mating profiles, original OMBR beam and gear component records, one hub, a supervised P0 bench source and cable, one smart motor, one distance sensor, reusable full electronic interface contracts and endpoint envelopes, P0 peripheral cables, a logical control source, a portable Python program, twin assets, and a simple controller binding. Artifact paths, mechanical dimensions, ratings, and digests are examples, not released hardware or measured evidence and do not claim compatibility with any third-party part.

protocols.name: OMBR deterministic-CBOR application layer over CAN FD P0
protocols.physicalLayer: ISO 11898-2 high-speed CAN physical layer using a qualified CAN FD transceiver
protocols.transport: CAN FD with bit-rate switching; Classic CAN nodes are not permitted on this segment
protocols.topology: Point-to-point independently switched hub-port segment; no passive branch in the example
protocols.addressing: Hub-assigned session node identifiers after presence detection and HELLO
protocols.arbitration: CAN identifier allocation remains P0 and must follow the released schema artifact
protocols.termination: 120 ohm at each physical end; endpoint implementation and validation are explicit
protocols.encoding: RFC 8949 Core Deterministic CBOR with definite lengths and unique map keys
protocols.framing: OMBR P0 header and CRC-32C envelope defined by section 8.4 and the schema artifact
protocols.startup: Presence, HELLO, DESCRIBE, validation, CONFIGURE, READY, then explicit ARM
protocols.timing: Interactive renewal at least every 50 ms; commands expire no later than 250 ms; exact bus budgets remain prototype evidence
protocols.errorHandling: Malformed, duplicate, stale, wrong-session, incompatible, or reserved state-changing frames are rejected without side effects; flooding isolates the port
protocols.versionNegotiation: Select highest shared major and then highest shared minor; no shared major leaves high power disabled
protocols.security: P0 relies on independently isolated point-to-point port segments; an authenticated shared-bus construction remains a stable-profile blocker

cableConstraints.shielding: Prototype uses an optional overall shield with drain terminated at the hub only; unshielded operation remains to be characterized.
cableConstraints.termination: 120 ohm at both endpoints; passive stubs and Y cables are forbidden.

hotPlug.attachSequence: Connector has no controlled first-mate contact; high power is electronically off, auxiliary power is current-limited, and contact bounce is validated before descriptor exchange.
hotPlug.disconnectBehavior: Presence loss or invalid traffic neutralizes commands and removes high power within the declared timeout.
hotPlug.unpoweredSignalBehavior: CAN and presence pins remain high impedance and within injection limits when either endpoint is unpowered.
hotPlug.highPowerDefault: Off until compatible contract, endpoint, cable, and source limits validate and the hub explicitly arms the port.

grounding.reference: CAN and presence use logic-return; high-power uses its dedicated return; returns join only at the documented hub power-domain point.
grounding.shieldTermination: Drain connects to hub chassis/EMC node only; it is open at the peripheral and never carries functional return current.
grounding.backfeedPolicy: No rail or signal may source an unpowered endpoint beyond the endpoint backfeed limit.

environment.derating: Prototype endpoint limits assume still air inside the stated enclosures and all adjacent contacts loaded; stable derating curves are not yet measured.

limitations: Micro-Fit P0 is limited to 30 documented mating cycles and is not a production connector.
Insertion force, retention force, signal-integrity margins, protection thresholds, and environmental derating are illustrative or unresolved.
This syntax example is not sufficient to build, arm, certify, or claim compatibility with hardware.

states.unpowered: All contacts high impedance; high-power and auxiliary switches de-energized.

states.armed: High power may enable within the validated envelope while heartbeat and limits remain healthy.
states.brownout: High power removes, commands neutralize, and re-arm is required.
states.shutdown: Commands neutralize, high power removes, then auxiliary power may remove after discharge.
states.fault: Affected port is isolated and latched or retried only as the fault matrix permits.
states.recovery: Healthy source, cleared fault, neutral commands, descriptor revalidation, and explicit re-arm are required.
